scope: UDP IPv4 payload-byte service descriptor ONLY. Not wire/checksum arithmetic, PCAP, full UDP, integrated stack or proof. Controller approval and independent fixed seeds still required before integration.
contract: IR0.2 flat-efsm-atomic-ordered-v1. Single READY state, no timers. No inheritance. All protocol policy explicit guard/actions. Use existing schema and supported operators only.

Initial checksums_enabled=true; app.configure_checksum changes it and emits nothing. app.send with ports0..65535 and data<=4096 octets emits exactly udp.send with identical data, length8+bytes_len(data), same ports and current checksum_enabled. Source port0 allowed. Invalid app fields uncovered; do not silently accept as no-op.

net.datagram source/destination/length/checksum are uint16 wire descriptors; data is already-decoded complete available IPv4 transport payload AFTER UDP8-byte header, including any trailing IP padding, with len(data)<=4096. Already-local IPv4 address context. Invalid metadata fields uncovered.

Receive bound port8080: length>=8 AND length<=8+bytes_len(data), and checksum==0 OR sum_valid, delivers data bytes_slice(data,0,length-8) and original ports. Other received datagrams in valid metadata domain silently discard, including bad nonzero checksum, short/overlong declared length, unbound port. Discard means zero emitted messages. Unbound-port ICMP is an explicit modeling gap; this temporary descriptor does not implement required full-endpoint error generation.

Duplicate valid datagrams deliver duplicate identical payloads. Empty/odd/nonzero/NUL payload content exact. No dedup or reliability promise. UDP length excludes IP padding. Supplied sum_valid is an assumption; no checksum computation/verification claim.

Retain delivered data in last_data bytes variable initialized[]. For discard leave it unchanged. Optional scalar counters supported, but independent oracles only fix literal emissions and READY/no timers. Invariants must express meaningful bounds on last_data length, not arbitrary true. Guards must be mutually exclusive with domain bounds<=4096 so unconstrained bytes beyond slice domain remain explicitly uncovered.
